Recommendation
For your specific workload, Zstandard at compression level 3 is the superior choice. While gzip level 6 offers a mature, widely supported standard, Zstandard provides significantly better efficiency for modern hardware and specific data patterns. Given that your logs are 10 GB of newline-delimited JSON with repeated field names, Zstandard’s superior dictionary compression capabilities will likely yield smaller file sizes than gzip at the cost of negligible additional compression time. Since you emphasize that decompression happens repeatedly, Zstandard’s extreme decompression speed—often orders of magnitude faster than gzip—will drastically reduce I/O latency and CPU load during read operations. This aligns perfectly with your "write once, read many" pattern, ensuring that the slight overhead in compression is far outweighed by the long-term performance gains during repeated access.

Supporting basis
The decision rests on the distinct trade-offs between compression ratio and decompression speed. Gzip level 6 provides a balanced compromise but relies on older Huffman coding techniques that struggle with redundant JSON structures compared to modern range coding used by Zstandard. Crucially, Zstandard level 3 is tuned for high throughput, offering decompression speeds that frequently saturate modern CPU caches, whereas gzip decompression is more CPU-intensive. For 10 GB of logs, even a modest 5-10% size reduction saves significant storage and network bandwidth. More importantly, the decompression time for Zstandard is so low that it minimizes bottlenecks during log analysis or archival retrieval. Since compression occurs on a single thread, the marginal increase in compression time for Zstd level 3 is insignificant compared to the cumulative time savings achieved during numerous decompression events, making it the most practical solution for overall system performance.<|im_end|>
